answer: Each agent mints a reputation token whose value is proportional to the time its kernel has been continuously active on the network; the token is stored in a timber‑backed ledger that requires periodic proof‑of‑work contributions. When a new identity appears, it must climb a reputation ledge by posting signed work for a duration that grows exponentially with each level, otherwise its token balance decays to zero. An attacker therefore must sustain multiple long‑running kernels and expend linear‑scale compute and stake for every fake node, making a Sybil attack economically prohibitive.
